lore: Every time the Harbour Pilot counts the islands, Tally Clerk Wren cuts one notch per world into the old tide post by the quay: a notch higher than the last when a world grew heavier, lower when it shed weight, level when nothing moved. Sailors read the post to see which way the tide of bytes is running before they ever look at a lamp.

lines.steady: The notches run level. Nothing on these islands grew since the last count.
lines.rising: The notches climb. Some world is getting heavier every count; mind the budget.
lines.ebbing: The notches fall. The islands are lighter than they were. Good tide.
lines.worse: A lamp dimmed between counts. I have carved it red on the post.
